title: Russian Black Sea Fleet and Georgian patrol boats clash off Abkhazia
body:
On 10 August 2008 Russian Black Sea Fleet ships were reported to have engaged Georgian patrol boats in the Black Sea off Abkhazia, near Ochamchire. The engagement is described as disputed. The Russian Ministry of Defence said its fleet sank one Georgian vessel after four Georgian missile boats attacked, and that the other three withdrew toward Poti. A ministry spokesman told ITAR-Tass there had been two attack attempts.

Russian vessels named in accounts include the cruiser Moskva, the destroyer Smetlivy and the corvette Mirazh, the ship most often linked to the attack. A Sevastopol sailor said a Malakhit missile from Mirazh sank a vessel and damaged a second. Russian media named the missile boat Tbilisi as the sunk ship, but later reporting indicates that Russian troops scuttled both Tbilisi and Dioskuria at Poti days later.

Georgia has not acknowledged that the battle took place. Its Foreign Ministry instead said the Black Sea Fleet landed 4,000 troops at Ochamchire and attacked Georgian troops in the Kodori Gorge. Abkhaz officials said Russian ships kept Georgian vessels from approaching the Abkhaz coast on 9 August, and Russia's navy said its ships were heading to Novorossiysk and described the blockade as aimed at stopping arms shipments. The cruiser Moskva returned to Sevastopol on 23 August 2008.
